subject: Availability & Support Redlines - Brightlane order form (uptime caps & maintenance gating)
messages:
From: Sami Patel <sami@brightlane.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightlane.com>
Date: 2028-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial SLA asks — uptime targets, credits, and maintenance windows

Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this through legal. We did an internal review of the draft order form and the main items procurement & engineering flagged are:

- Uptime target: you have 99.95% in the order form; our ops policy needs 99.99% for customer-facing APIs.
- Service credits: we need a clearer sliding scale tied to monthly downtime minutes rather than a single bucket; also prefer a maximum credit cap at 30% of monthly fees.
- Response times: request 1-hour P1 response & 4-hour P2 response during business hours (P1/P2 definitions attached).
- Maintenance windows: prefer maintenance requiring more than 4 hours notice for any blackout; want a monthly blackout cap of 6 hours and notification 72 hours in advance.

We attached our proposed SLA doc for reference. Can Redwood confirm which items are negotiable vs which require an exception? Happy to join a short call this week.

Thanks,
Sami Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager — Brightlane
[Attachment: Brightlane_proposed_sla_v2.pdf (pdf, 78KB)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sami Patel <sami@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Contracts <contracts@brightlane.com>
Date: 2028-05-01T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA asks — uptime targets, credits, and maintenance windows

Sami — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Marissa (AM) and Lauren (legal) to coordinate redlines. High-level responses below; attached a marked-up order form and a simple credit model we used to run the math.

Highlights from Redwood:
- Uptime: We can support 99.99% for single-region deployments on Dedicated plans (this would require a dedicated capacity commitment). For hosted accounts, our standard is 99.95% with multi-region fallback options.
- Credits: We propose a staircase credit model (see attached SLA_Credit_Model.xlsx) tied to cumulative monthly downtime in minutes with a cap at 50% of monthly fees for hosted tiers; for Dedicated we can discuss a 30% cap per your request.
- Response times: We can offer 1-hour P1 on Enterprise/ Dedicated, 2-hour P1 on hosted standard. P2 remains 4 hours. Will ask Aditya to confirm ops runbook constraints.
- Maintenance: We already have a 72-hour notification for non-emergency maintenance, and monthly maintenance windows typically do not exceed 4 hours per region. For blackout caps >4 hours we will need explicit contractual carveouts; propose adding an exception bucket for planned long cutovers with additional credits if exceeded.

Next steps: Lauren, can you review the attached redlines and call out any ingestion risks or language changes procurement will need? Marissa, can you confirm the Dedicated commitment thresholds for 99.99% availability and the pricing lift? Sami — if these high-level tradeoffs look reasonable, let's schedule a 30-minute call (Marissa will propose slots).

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
[Attachments: Brightlane_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf, SLA_Credit_Model.xlsx]

Date: 2028-05-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA asks — uptime targets, credits, and maintenance windows

Quick operational notes (copying Sami so Brightlane has transparency):

- Dedicated vs Hosted: The 99.99% commitment requires both Dedicated capacity and multi-AZ deployment; the rough uplift from our pricing team is ~1.6x list for the committed pool. I will pull the formal quote once we have a term length.

- Credit model: We recommend the staircase approach Evelyn attached, but to be customer-friendly propose (example):
  - 99.95–99.99%: 10% credit
  - 99.9–99.95%: 25% credit
  - <99.9%: 50% credit (cap)
  - Cap: 30% for Dedicated / 50% for standard hosted (we can set separate caps per SKU)

- Response times & P definitions: Aditya, can you confirm SLA runbook for 1-hr P1 on Dedicated (follow-up: on-call rotation, follow-the-sun escalation)? We need to ensure the commitments are operationally feasible and documented in the runbook if we put them in the Order Form.

- Maintenance: We can support a 72-hour notice for non-emergency ops; for planned >4hr blackouts we need a rolling schedule and the ability to gate via a change window — otherwise we surface significant risk.

Proposed call agenda for the sync with Brightlane: 1) confirm target availability and whether they want Dedicated; 2) walk through credit staircase & caps; 3) alignment on P1/P2 defs and runbook; 4) finalize notice windows and carveouts. 30 minutes should do it.

—Marissa
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-05-05T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA asks — uptime targets, credits, and maintenance windows

Evelyn / Marissa — thanks for the quick follow-up and the redlines. A few counterpoints from procurement and engineering after reviewing your model:

1) Cap: Brightlane is willing to accept a 50% cap for hosted tiers but requests a 30% cap for Dedicated (we're aligned there). We'd like that explicitly split in the order form rather than leaving it to SKU tables.
2) Staircase thresholds: procurement prefers thresholds based on cumulative outage minutes (we included a short table in the attached procurement note). If you can reflect that window-to-credit mapping in the Order Form it'll help doc automation on our side.
3) Response times: we can accept 2-hour P1 for hosted if committed to multi-region fallback within 15 minutes of failover; otherwise we need 1-hour on Dedicated.
4) Maintenance gating: we can accept a monthly 8-hour planned maintenance cap if Redwood provides a monthly rolling schedule and a single point-of-contact for emergency approvals.

We're OK to proceed to legal redline exchange if Redwood sends a clean MSA/Order Form with the Dedicated option called out and the credit staircase table inline. Can you propose a few times for a legal + procurement call (Lauren + Rafael + our contracts counsel)?

Thanks,
Sami Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager — Brightlane
[Attachment: Brightlane_procurement_note_v1.docx (docx, 24KB)]
